factPack.central_question: Who decides how long your traffic light stays green?
factPack.audience_promise: Answer one precise question about urban traffic control network using only documented evidence.

verified_facts.text: When control fails, signals fall back to fixed timings and queues grow.
Detectors measure traffic and software adjusts green times and offsets in real time.
Why 63,000 intersections share one control system.
SCATS runs signals in over 216 cities.
Australia alone has around 11,000 of them.
Sensors in the road feed real-time timing changes.
Smarter offsets improved flow by 8% in one test.
Better pedestrian timing cut unsafe crossing by 34%.
That's why your green light is decided by software.
SCATS is installed at more than 63,000 intersections in over 216 cities in 33 countries.
verified_facts.source: Wikipedia — Sydney Coordinated Adaptive Traffic System

verified_facts.text: In Australia, where the system was first developed, the majority of signalised intersections are SCATS operated (around 11,000).
verified_facts.source: Wikipedia — Sydney Coordinated Adaptive Traffic System

verified_facts.text: Longer or more frequent green signals for pedestrians can reduce unsafe crossing by 34%.
verified_facts.source: Wikipedia — Sydney Coordinated Adaptive Traffic System

verified_facts.text: The new method of on-line offset calculation showed an 8% improvement over the existing precalculated offset plans.

verified_facts.text: City traffic flow depends on adaptive control systems coordinating signals.
Local controllers keep running basic plans if central control drops.
Traffic management is a key branch within logistics.
It concerns the planning, control and purchasing of transport services needed to physically move vehicles (for example aircraft, road vehicles, rolling stock and watercraft) and freight.

hook_candidates: A city’s traffic grid collapses into chaos the moment the central computer blinks out—watch the domino effect unfold.

paragraphs.text: Why 63,000 intersections share one control system.
SCATS is deployed at more than 63,000 intersections across 216 cities in 33 countries, and in its home country Australia it operates the majority of signalised intersections, about 11,000.

The system coordinates signals adaptively, and an online offset calculation method improves performance by 8% over precalculated plans; longer or more frequent pedestrian greens can reduce unsafe crossings by 34%.
The scope covers planning, controlling, and purchasing transport services required to physically move vehicles—road vehicles, aircraft, rail stock, watercraft—and freight.
